title: Client onboarding sprint map and failure fuzz notes
content:
Purpose:
This note sketches a 4-week sprint map for an SDK-first client onboarding experience, with a heavy focus on failure-mode fuzzing and a minimal telemetry contract so we can ship predictable sample apps quickly. It is intentionally pragmatic: prioritize high-signal smoke tests, reproducible demos, and obvious recovery paths for end users integrating Redwood APIs.

Audience:
- Developer advocates and SDK engineers running the onboarding sprint
- Solutions engineers who will use the checklist in customer calls
- Documentation writers responsible for the quickstart page and Troubleshooting sidebar

Success metrics (measureable):
- Time to first successful generation from a fresh repo (goal: < 10 minutes)
- % of onboarding runs that pass the smoke checklist (goal: 90% on first try)
- Number of unique failure scenarios reproducible by CI fuzz harness (goal: 12 scenarios)
- Reduction in support tickets for "initial setup" by 35% after rollout

Sprint overview (4-week plan):
Week 0 (prep):
- Finalize telemetry contract (events, minimal attributes)
- Author 2 lightweight sample apps (node + python) that follow the same flow: init API key -> hello generate -> stream -> embed -> fallback
- Create CI harness template that can run the smoke checklist in GH Actions

Week 1 (quickstart polish):
- Consolidate Quickstart README: single-file steps + copy-pastable snippets
- Add explicit env var guidance for common cloud shells
- Create lightweight Dockerfile for reproducible local environment

Week 2 (fuzz harness and failure matrix):
- Implement a fuzz-runner that can inject: slow network, TCP resets, 500s from API, truncated streaming frames, corrupted JSON responses
- Map 12 targeted scenarios (list below) and write deterministic regression tests for each

Week 3 (telemetry + observability):
- Hook sample apps to the minimal telemetry contract and send to a staging funnel 
- Create telemetry dashboard template (latency, first-try-success, fallback-used, retry-count)
- Author troubleshooting guide entries for the most common failure modes

Week 4 (docs + handoff):
- Consolidate notes into a single Quickstart doc page and a short video script (3–4 min)
- Run an internal playtest with one SE and one engineer unfamiliar with SDKs; iterate
- Tag and merge required PRs, update changelog

Onboarding flow (happy path):
1) Sign up (or use sandbox key)
2) Install SDK (npm/pip)
3) Set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var
4) Run hello-console sample (single request) -> expect: code 200 + text response
5) Try streaming example for partial output + graceful cancel
6) Use embed endpoint and validate vector shape (length, dtype) with included helper
7) Copy sample app to a project and run smoke checklist

Smoke checklist (CI-friendly):
- [ ] env var present (REDWOOD_API_KEY)
- [ ] sdk install succeeded (exit 0)
- [ ] hello request returns 200 and contains at least 8 tokens
- [ ] streaming request yields incremental frames and final commit
- [ ] embedding returns array with expected length and non-empty floats
- [ ] retry path exercised: simulate 500 on first try and validate automatic retry returns valid output
- [ ] fallback route exercised: configure small model variant and confirm fallback used when high-latency or quota errors present

Failure fuzz scenarios (target list, CRITICAL FOR CI):
1) Transient network latency (p50->p95 increased by 5x)
2) Complete network partition for 3s during streaming response
3) API returns 502/503 intermittently on token 1024 (verify retry semantics)
4) Partial body delivered (truncated JSON) for streaming final chunk
5) Corrupted metadata header (invalid content-length)
6) Excessively large payload (simulate model returning 1M tokens) -> graceful abort path
7) Auth key malformed -> clear error message mapping
8) Rate limit (429) under burst load -> backoff + quota guidance
9) Model mismatch: client expects chat but server returns text-only response
10) Embedding shape mismatch (old client expecting 256 but new model 384)
11) HSM/KMS transient unavailability when using private deployment keys
12) Local cache corruption (prefix cache invalid deserialization)

Telemetry contract (minimal, pragmatic):
- event:start_onboard (fields: sdk_lang, sample_id, env, sdk_version, correlation_id)
- event:quickstart_step (fields: step_name, duration_ms, success_bool, error_code?)
- event:fallback_triggered (fields: reason, original_model, fallback_model, latency_ms)
- event:smoke_check_result (fields: check_name, pass_bool, details)
Notes: keep payloads small, do not send full prompts or embeddings. Use hashed IDs for correlation.

Sample snippets (copy-paste ready):
- CURL hello (minimal):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"Say hi in 5 words"}'

- Node (minimal):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
(async ()=>{
  const r = await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-mini', input: 'Hello, name a color' });
  console.log(r.text);
})();

- Python (minimal):
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='gpt-mini', input='Short poem')
print(resp.text)

Developer-facing troubleshooting snippets:
- If streaming frames never finish: check proxy or HTTP library (some HTTP client libs buffer by default). Reproduce with curl --no-buffer.
- If embedding length mismatch: print model info endpoint (GET /v1/models/:id) to confirm vector dim. Add explicit matrix check in quickstart.

CI harness notes:
- Use a local stub server (small node process) that can emulate the 12 fuzz scenarios; we already have an internal repo stub-server. Link: https://github.com/redwood-internal/stub-server (TODO: make public sample)
- GH Actions job matrix: node, python, docker -> run smoke checklist + one randomized fuzz per job (seeded)

Hand-off checklist for PRs: (owner creates the PRs and tags reviewers)
- SDK sample repo: add smoke.yml GH Actions job -> reviewer: Priya
- Docs: quickstart.md + troubleshooting page -> reviewer: Docs team (DOCS-678)
- Telemetry: event schema in internal events repo -> reviewer: Observability (Samir)
- Stub server: add deterministic fuzz flags -> reviewer: Liam

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we include a tiny local binary to simulate high-latency (yes recommended)
- Can we publish the stub-server as an 'official' dev dependency? Pros: reproducibility. Cons: maintenance burden.
- Should quickstart auto-collect telemetry opt-in by default? Lean: opt-in, but show one-click opt-in in readme.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Pair with SE for a live run in Week 3 and capture video of failure modes.
- Add compact diagrams showing "happy path" vs "fallback path" in docs (one svg).
- Draft a 2-page cheat sheet for field SEs with commands they can paste into customer terminals.

Rough PR references and links: 
- github PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/214 (sample app + CI)
- jira: ENG-1423 (onboarding sprint epic)
- docs ticket: DOCS-678 (quickstart rewrite)

End of note.

(Informal; expect to iterate heavily. Treat this as a working artifact.)
